clauses.text:
By virtue of and pursuant to the 
authority vested in me by section 5 of the 
act of February 8, 1887, 24 Stat. 388, 389, 
by the act of June "21, 1906, 34 Stat. 325, 
326, and by the act of March 2, 1917, 39 
Stat. 969, 976, and other applicable pro­
visions of law, it is hereby ordered that 
the periods of trust or other restrictions 
against alienation contained in any pat­
ent applying to Indian lands, whether of 
a tribal or individual status, which, un­
less extended, will expire during the 
calendar year 1947, be, and they are 
hereby, extended for a further period of 
twenty-five years from the date on which 
any such trust would otherwise expire.
This order is not intended to apply to 
any case in which the Congress has 
specifically reserved to itself authority to 
extend the period of trust on tribal or 
individual Indian lands.

status_research.rationale: I read the complete held EO 9811 (11 FR 14483, Dec. 17, 1946; the held extract also carries unrelated neighbouring Federal Register items). It is one operative sentence: under the 1887, 1906 and 1917 acts, trust or restriction periods against alienation in Indian-land patents that 'unless extended, will expire during the calendar year 1947' are 'extended for a further period of twenty-five years from the date on which any such trust would otherwise expire', excluding cases where Congress reserved the extension authority. It acts once on a closed class (periods expiring in 1947) and grants a fixed 25-year extension, so by its own term the extension it creates runs out no later than December 31, 1972; it contains no continuing command and no savings clause. The held own-term record TERM:EO:9811 (the 25-year operative sentence, read in the held full text) is the basis. The 1989 Codification row reads 'Authority maintained at departmental level (see EO 10250)', which I treat as a lead that the extension authority was later delegated to the Department of the Interior, not as a statement that EO 9811 itself is in force; EO 10250 is not held and I did not examine it. Whether specific trusts were later extended by Interior orders or statute is a separate question and does not make the 1946 presidential order itself a continuing command. Partial scope: only the 1947-expiring class and not congressionally reserved cases; the end applies to the whole order. This is a provisional NO hypothesis only; the exact last expiry date and any effect of EO 10250 or later statutes remain lifecycle gaps.

reviews.rationale: I read the full held EO 9811 (11 FR 14483, official FR text; neighbouring items ignored). Its single operative sentence extends trust or alienation-restriction periods expiring during calendar 1947 'for a further period of twenty-five years from the date on which any such trust would otherwise expire', excluding cases Congress reserved. The order acts once on a closed class and fixes its own duration, so the extensions it made ran out no later than the end of 1972; it contains no continuing command. I tried to refute the NO: any later continuation of particular trusts (later extension orders, departmental action under the authority delegated by EO 10250, or statutes extending trust periods indefinitely) would be a new act under other authority, not continued operation of EO 9811; the 1989 Codification line points to EO 10250 as a delegation lead, not to EO 9811 being in force. The held TERM record is from the official FR text, not the APP copy. Independent view NO (expired by own term); I agree, while recording that this is a 'spent by own term' NO rather than an express revocation and the exact last expiry and the EO 10250 delegation are lifecycle gaps. Nonauthoritative AI hypothesis.
